subject: Discovery recap: FastRetail PoC & integration plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tan <michael.tan@fastretail.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: FastRetail PoC & integration plan

Thanks for your time today, Michael — really helpful to hear about the roadmap and the operational constraints as you scale chat and search across stores. Quick recap of what we captured and proposed next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points
- Current latency spikes at peak retail hours (3–5x baseline) causing poor UX for store associates.
- High per-query cost on current hosted embeddings service; limited caching/batching.
- Data residency and audit requirements for PII in agent logs.

Current stack
- Frontend: React web + internal POS system; backend services in Node/TypeScript and Python.
- Embeddings & semantic search: hosted vendor (proprietary API).
- Hosting: GCP us-west and us-east.

Success criteria for PoC
- Consistent p95 inference latency under 400ms for typical queries (<=256 tokens).
- 30%+ token-cost reduction via batching + prefix caching compared to current baseline.
- Integration that meets your compliance checklist (audit logs, retention policies).

Proposed PoC scope & timeline
1) Week 0 (this week): Align on PoC goals, data access model, and owners (this email).
2) Week 1–2: Tech deep-dive & SDK test — ingest a representative prompt set; confirm latency/cost baseline.
3) Week 3–4: Pilot on a small subset of traffic (internal beta), collect metrics and qualitative feedback.
4) Week 5: Review results and decide Dedicated vs Hosted deployment.

Milestones & owners
- Tech deep-dive / integration plan: Dylan Brooks (solutions engineer) — to confirm SDK choices and endpoint config.
- Security/compliance checklist: Marissa Cole (customer ops).
- Program owner / exec sponsor: Michael Tan (FastRetail).

Integration notes (initial)
- SDKs: Python and Node supported; recommend Python for batch data ingestion scripts and Node SDK for service integration in your Node services.
- API compatibility: REST + SDKs; streaming supported for chat.
- Data controls: We can enable customer-managed KMS and configure per-tenant audit logs for PoC.

Attachments: FastRetail-MAP-draft.pdf (map with milestones and success metrics). I added a HubSpot link to the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/53421/FD-2026-007.

Next steps
- Michael / Sara: confirm internal stake-holders and whether you can share a small sample prompt set for benchmarking (anonymized).
- Dylan: propose two slots for the tech deep-dive next week.

Appreciate the time — will follow up with a calendar invite once we lock the tech call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

1) Data retention — for the PoC we need a 90-day rolling retention window and an exportable audit log. Will Redwood support that?
2) For benchmarking, we can share anonymized prompt/response pairs from the last 30 days (approx. 5k queries).
3) For the tech deep-dive please include a short section on how model fallbacks are handled during capacity constraints (we saw timeouts from our current provider).

We're keen to move quickly. I'm available Tue/Wed next week after 11am PT for the deep-dive.

Adding a few technical notes to address Michael's questions and prep for the deep-dive: 

- Retention/audit: We can configure a 90-day retention window for PoC and generate an exportable audit log (JSON lines) scoped to the tenant. We'll need to confirm whether FastRetail wants logs pushed to their GCS bucket or to pull via API.
- Fallbacks: Redwood supports model variant routing and automatic fallback to a lower-tier compatible model with graceful degradation + request queuing. We can demonstrate the fallback path and the failure-mode behavior in the deep-dive.
- SDK recommendation: Node SDK for your production services (low-latency streaming) + Python for bulk ingestion. For the PoC I propose we provide a small Python benchmark script (open-source sample) that runs your 5k anonymized queries and returns latency/cost metrics.
- Auth & keys: For PoC we'll use scoped API keys tied to the FastRetail org id; later we can switch to customer-managed KMS for Dedicated.

I can draft the benchmark script and bring sample results from a similar retail PoC. Ben, I'll propose two slots for Tue/Wed 11:30am and 2:30pm PT.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
